source.prompt: A California ground squirrel (Otospermophilus beecheyi) walking on all four legs like a squirrel crossing a lawn: NOT sitting, NOT standing up, NOT a prairie dog, NOT a marmot, NOT a chipmunk. Single adult, side-on, body horizontal and long, back level, all four paws flat on the ground, front legs straight down under the shoulders, head held up and forward. Realistic proportions: head and body 26 cm, body a little heavier than a tree squirrel's but not fat, short legs, rounded head, small erect rounded ears, blunt muzzle, open dark eyes. Bushy flattened tail 18 cm long (two thirds of the body), wider than the hind leg, held straight out behind and level, not curled. Mottled grey-brown fur, pale grey shoulders, buff belly. No base, no ground. Game-ready, symmetric.

tiers.note: Whiskers and fur shards removed (inward ray thickness); the generated strand tail removed at the rump and a new one lofted from the same root: 0.18 m, held out behind rising 14-26 degrees, 1.7 times wider than deep past the base, lumpy outline, mottled core, darker band, pale buff-grey fringe faces; head raised 8 degrees about the neck (alert); closed eyes replaced by a dark eye in a wide whitish ring (lod0 a small octahedron in painted ring faces, lod1 one dark face in the ring, lod2 none); recoloured by region with per-face buff and dusky flecks hashed from position. Triangles: lod0 2,000 = 1,744 body + 240 tail (10 sides x 12 rings) + 16 eyes; lod1 600 = 516 + 84 tail (6 x 7); lod2 200 = 168 + 32 tail (4 x 4). Suggested switches 12 and 40 m (the gray squirrel's). GLB 198,960 bytes. Area-weighted mean of the up-facing body faces sRGB #7e7163 (lighter than the brief's back #6e5e4c because the pale mantle and buff flecks count).

rig: rodent rig template (as RIG.squirrel in client/src/animalModels.js; not wired yet): PART BODY 0 hindquarters, CHEST 7 (lumbar pivot; bound flex, sit-up), HEAD 6 (base of the neck) and LEG_A 1 (fore pair, elbows) as children of the chest, LEG_B 2 (hind pair, stifles), TAIL 3 and TAIL_TIP 8 (child of the tail). Pivots in extras.rig (three.js metres): chest [0, 0.1001, -0.0487], head [0, 0.0744, 0.0869], fore [±0.0229, 0.0349, 0.0514], hind [±0.0279, 0.0268, -0.093], tail [0, 0.0663, -0.0923], tail_tip [0, 0.0888, -0.1716].
rig_notes: Proposed RIG constants for the wiring lane (checked by posing the GLB with the shader's math in Blender, not yet in the client): amp [0.9, 0.5, 0.35, 0] as the gray squirrel; pose [0.4, -0.3, 1.05, 0] (legs squashed to 0.4 on pose, the tail lowered 0.3 rad to lie out behind on the ground, the head pitched 1.05 rad back down so it looks level); drop 0.016 m (hind pivot 0.027 m x (1 - 0.4), so the rump sits on the ground); k { spine 0.2, spinePhase 1.2, sit 1.25 (72 degrees: bolt upright, leaning a little forward like the photos), foreFold 2.2 (the fore legs reach forward at rest, so they need more than the sit to hang against the chest), tipLag 0.6, tipWave 0.25, tipCurl 0.2, abduct 0 }. The sentinel is the commonest sight, so pose 1 should be held for long spells at the burrow mouth.

candidates.review: Reads as a ground squirrel at once: long low body on short legs, broad rounded head with a blunt muzzle, small rounded erect ears, all four feet flat (fore legs angled forward, hind feet under the rump). Faults: the tail is a fan of hair strands rising at 40 degrees (replaced); whiskers and flat fur shards on the neck and chest as strands (removed); eyes modelled as closed slits (replaced); the body is a little long and low for a standing squirrel (fine for one walking). Topology: 19,627 triangles, most of them in the tail strands and whiskers (about 4,500 left for the body), 6 islands; 1.89 units long, +z up, nose toward -y.

accuracy_notes: Adopted 2026-10-26 from the second Meshy preview. What reads as a ground squirrel rather than the western gray: a longer, lower, heavier body on short legs; a broad blunt head with small ears; a tail about two thirds of head and body, moderately bushy and flattened (1.7:1, against the gray's 2.2:1 plume as long as the body), held out behind rather than up; a mottled grey-brown coat with buff and dusky flecks instead of clean silver; the pale silver-grey mantle on the shoulders and sides of the neck with a darker band down the back; a wide whitish eye ring; a buff belly, not white; and the sentinel sit-up, which the rig poses bolt upright. Not yet in any tile's species.json (GBIF has it on all three tiles: 8, 5 and 1 occurrences), not in index.json and not wired in animals.js / animalModels.js (the wiring lane adds it). Still open: the dark band and mantle V read only from above and close; the tail is procedural (the generated one was hair strands); the fore legs hang as thin sticks when sitting (no paws held to the chest); the sit is two rigid parts (hindquarters and chest), so the belly line bends at the lumbar; colours are by region, not a texture. A local naturalist should check the tail length and bushiness, the mantle, and how upright the sentinel is.
